lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Privilege gateway model routes
steps.what: The gateway writes one log line per model call with provider, model, token counts, a cost estimate, latency, user and key ID.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Virtual key
steps.what: A virtual key is an LLM-scoped agent key created in the Agent Registry wizard.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Real provider key held in Privilege and injec…
steps.what: It needs the real provider key in hand: Privilege stores that key, does not return it on read, and injects it server-side.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Allowed-models list
steps.what: Each key is bound to one provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint) and carries an owner, an allowed-models list, request and token rate limits, a budget, an expiry, scopes and AI Guard settings.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Gateway log
steps.what: The application calls the gateway's route for its provider and presents the virtual key as a bearer token or API-key header.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Cluster-wide spend limits
steps.what: Spend limits are budgets in US dollars or tokens on a daily, weekly, monthly or lifetime window, aggregated across every gateway instance so a limit holds cluster-wide, with requests and tokens per minute capped per key.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Tenant model pricing
steps.what: Tenant model pricing lets a tenant override the built-in per-model rates, or add models the platform does not price, so cost reflects the contract.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Usage accounting
steps.what: The usage record captures metadata only by default, and prompt and response content is not written to the audit log by default; full retention is an explicit tenant policy, encrypted to a key only the tenant holds.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.

steps.title: Metadata-only usage records
steps.what: Every request records the model, prompt and completion tokens, calculated cost, latency and status, streaming or not.
steps.why: Applications and agents should never hold a model provider's API key.
